counterfactual_text: The approaching tennis ball reverses direction while still separated from the racket; racket contact occurs afterward.
positive_text: The approaching tennis ball visibly contacts the racket, compresses briefly, and then travels back in the opposite direction.
semantic_text: A tennis racket strikes an approaching tennis ball, sending the same ball back in the opposite direction. Initial scene: A fixed side view of one tennis racket and one tennis ball in a simple tennis practice setting. The ball is several ball diameters in front of the center of the racket face on a clear horizontal alignment, with both objects fully visible, unobstructed, and framed at a useful medium scale. Required visible entities: one tennis racket; one tennis ball. At the beginning: racket: intact with its full face visible; tennis ball: intact and spatially separated from the racket face. Required layout: ball center aligns with the central racket-face region; clear visible space separates the ball and racket; the interaction line and return-direction space remain inside the frame. Required state changes: ball position: approaches and contacts the racket; ball deformation: brief contact compression; ball direction: incoming to outgoing opposite direction. These event variables are allowed to change: ball position; ball travel direction; brief ball deformation at contact. Preserve throughout: static side-view camera; racket identity; tennis-ball identity and color; one tennis racket; one tennis ball; the same ball before and after contact.
